question: As part of the project to dredge the port of Trapani1 that is currently under way, the material dredged from the seabed of the port is being deposited 2.5 miles off the coast, close to Natura 2000 site ITA010025 – ‘Seabed of the Gulf of Custonaci’, and risks damaging the site’s biodiversity.

The fishers’ association ‘PrinciPesca’ has complained to the harbourmaster’s office in Trapani about the presence of sludge (probably containing hydrocarbons) right in the fishing area above the Gulf of Custonaci, where the deposit is taking place. The dredging works, managed by the Port Authority of Western Sicily, were assigned some EUR 60 million under the national recovery and resilience plan (NRRP).

Aside from running counter to environmental requirements2, unloading excavated earth into the sea could cause serious damage to site ITA010025, marine biocoenosis, fish stocks and fisheries. The technical report from the Municipality of San Vito Lo Capo found irregularities, missing documentation and incomplete analyses in the environmental impact assessment and procedures related to the dumping.
3 Can the Commission: 1.
ask the relevant national and regional authorities to urgently check whether the works are being carried out in accordance with Directive 2000/60/EC?
clarify whether the issues raised in the technical report constitute a breach of Directive 92/43/EEC (Habitats Directive)4?
provide an assessment of the eligibility for NRRP financing, in view of the potential violation of the ‘do no significant harm’ and precautionary principles?

CUP I94D19000000005 CNP NRRP – PORT OF TRAPANI – WORKS TO DREDGE THE OUTER HARBOUR AND AREAS TO THE WEST OF THE RONCIGLIO SPIT. Ministry of the Environment Decree No 173 of 15 July 2016 – Regulation laying down procedures and technical criteria for authorisation to release material excavated from the seabed into the sea, and technical annex.

The annex to this technical report details the way in which the environmental impact assessment and project paperwork fail to properly document: alternative sites at which to dump the dredged material; instructions for transport and dumping; alternative solutions to dumping at sea. Details are also very patchy on the fisheries activities taking place on this seabed.

The technical report was submitted to the Port Authority for comment and the Municipality of San Vito Lo Capo for rebuttal. National impact assessment guidelines – Methodological guidance for Article 6(3) and (4) of the Habitats Directive.
